title: Macro Maths Mission
welcome_lead: The Chancellor needs your help. Plug in the numbers, calculate aggregate demand and forecast UK economic activity.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics calculations adventure on AD components, multipliers and balancing injections and withdrawals.
final_note: You can balance a national economy. Onwards to global trade!

concepts.def: How an injection ripples into a bigger rise in output.
Marginal propensity to consume — share of new income spent.
Marginal propensity to save — share of new income saved.
Government spends more than it raises in tax.

walkthroughs.body_html: Take consumer spend £700bn + investment £180bn + government £220bn + exports £450bn − imports £400bn. Sum: 700+180+220+50 = £1,150bn. That's aggregate demand for the year. Notice net exports (X − M) = £50bn here.

If the government injects £10bn into roads and workers spend 80% of new income (MPC = 0.8), the multiplier = 1 / (1 − 0.8) = 5. So £10bn injection raises GDP by £50bn. Useful for thinking about fiscal stimulus.

If the government spends £900bn but only collects £820bn in tax, the budget deficit is £80bn. To cover it, the Treasury issues bonds (borrows). Persistent deficits raise the national debt — a big GCSE evaluation point.
